explanation: Start from standard form y = ax² + bx + c and convert without changing the graph. The vertex x is always h = −b/2a (and k = f(h)), which is why the dashed axis of symmetry tracks b and a. To reach factored form you need the roots, and the discriminant b² − 4ac decides whether they exist: ≥ 0 gives the two green crossings from the quadratic formula, < 0 means it can't factor over the reals. Adjust a, b, c and watch all three forms describe the same single curve.
bullets: Vertex from standard form: h = −b/2a, then k = f(h).
Discriminant b² − 4ac < 0 means no real factoring — vertex form still works.
